title: No shell/CLI helper to call an MCP tool against the running daemon for smoke tests
wanted_capability: A one-shot way to invoke an MCP tool (initialize → tools/call) against the running blackboxd from the shell — e.g. `bro mcp call <tool> '<json-args>'` — so an agent that rebuilds and restarts the daemon can smoke-test the live MCP surface (confirm a tool is registered and round-trips) without hand-rolling the JSON-RPC handshake.
missing_primitive: bro mcp call / bro mcp tools-list (shell MCP client for the local daemon)
fallback_used: Hand-rolled curl: POST /mcp initialize, scraped the Mcp-Session-Id response header, then POSTed tools/list and tools/call with that header and parsed the SSE/JSON by hand to confirm bbox_gap was registered and filed a gap end-to-end.
evidence: session: gap-notes first-class deploy smoke test
fallback: curl initialize + Mcp-Session-Id + tools/call against http://127.0.0.1:7264/mcp
notes: bbox_mcp_surface(action="replay") shows tools visible under a surface packet, but there's no plain "call this tool / list registered tools" client for verifying a daemon redeploy from the shell. Recurs for anyone who rebuilds blackboxd and wants to confirm the tool surface before trusting it.
resolution_note: Implemented `bro mcp call <tool> '<json>'` (commit 7c2771a on beta/blackbox-v2, crates/bro-cli/src/mcp_call.rs + main.rs wiring). Does the streamable-HTTP MCP handshake (initialize → tools/call) against the local daemon, propagates Mcp-Session-Id, SSE-aware response decode, prints the tool result. Validated live: `bro mcp call bbox_stats '{}'` returned real corpus stats (105448 docs, 465MB index). Dispatched to a fleet bro (brodex) during the autonomous dogfood loop (thread-c38e005d).
